findings.desc: CHK-015:edge:1 (matcher count bound is policy-resolved, not hardcoded): no fixture in red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs or the smoke validates the matcher-count bound under a policy with a DIFFERENT policy.maxMatchers value. Every other floor claim of this kind in the same story (rule-2 length/entropy floors in red-w2d-specificity-conjunction.mjs via a raised-minMatcherLen policy, the class registry in CHK-016 via a CUSTOM matcherClassRegistry, policyDigest content-sensitivity in CHK-010 via an otherPolicy) IS proven with a two-policy differential; only the CHK-015 count bound is proven solely against the frozen default (maxMatchers=8), so a hard-coded 8 in place of policy.maxMatchers would pass every committed test. The binder self-flagged this exact gap in its own evidence note.

CHK-012 read-only claim (packages/main/tests/red/red-w2d-command-readonly.mjs, packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts section 7): the handler doc comment on red_evidence_envelope_check (packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts ~line 349) asserts the command spawns no RED run and its only child processes are the W2b binding readers git rev-parse/git show. No committed test verifies this: the mechanism used (a per-file SHA-256 snapshot of .lattice/ taken before and after the call) can only detect writes under .lattice/; it does not intercept, mock, or otherwise observe child_process.spawn/exec/spawnSync calls, so a regression that caused the handler to shell out to run a test (e.g. code drifted toward the reserved-for-later runner leaf) would pass this regression undetected even though it violates the storys core before a run is ever spent safety property. Given this is the single most safety-critical claim of the whole command, the read-only regression should intercept/spy on child_process to positively prove no RED-run-shaped spawn occurs, not rely solely on directory-hash absence-of-evidence.

CHK-013:happy:0 literal intent text reads: red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts listed in lattice.config.json validate.commands and lattice validate runs it successfully. The bound evidence (packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-validate-registration.mjs) only statically enumerates dist/tasks/red-evidence-* on disk and cross-checks it against the validate.commands array in config; it never invokes the lattice validate command itself. CHK-013:happy:1 separately runs the smoke by direct node invocation (node packages/main/dist/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.js), not through the lattice validate pipeline. So no committed evidence in this story exercises the actual validate-pipeline invocation path (spawn args/cwd/timeout handling for this entry) end to end; the binder self-flagged this exact gap (lattice validate was not run for this binding). Registration-in-config + direct-invocation-passes only jointly approximate the literal intent, and this exact substitution pattern was previously used for the same reason in W2c (red-w2c-validate-registration.mjs), so it is a known, repeated, but still real gap against the literal command the intent names.

CHK-002 closed-enum rejections (stream, polarity, greenExempt legality) and CHK-001 identity/kind rejections are exercised only against kind:literal-line matchers across red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs and the smoke; no fixture asserts an invalid stream, invalid polarity, or illegal greenExempt on a kind:class matcher. In envelope.ts these checks (validateAssertionEnvelope lines ~317-337) run unconditionally before the kind-specific branch, so the current implementation is not actually kind-differentiated, but the committed matrix does not prove that: a future change that moved these checks inside the literal-line-only branch (mirroring how value-byte-length checks are correctly literal-line-only) would silently stop rejecting a malformed class matcher stream/polarity/greenExempt, and no committed test would catch it.

packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts:346-348 (matcher-value-empty) tags an EMPTY literal-line value as R1-3. Spec places non-emptiness under §1.3 rule 1 ("value MUST be stored trimmed (§1.1.1), MUST be non-empty, and MUST NOT be a member of policy.forbiddenCatchAlls", spec:401-403), which is the §1.3 minimum-specificity rule that R1-2 owns ("a degenerate/blocklisted literal", spec:495-498). R1-3s own enumerated list (spec:499-504) explicitly names only value longer than maxMatcherLen or carrying leading/trailing whitespace for value-bound failures — it never mentions empty/too-short. The codebase itself already applies this exact reasoning to the two sibling clauses of the same rule-1 triple: trimmed -> R1-3 (explicitly named in R1-3s list) and blocklisted -> R1-2 (explicitly named in R1-2s list, per envelope.ts:393-400). non-empty is the third clause and is NOT named in R1-3s list, so by the codes own established methodology it should route to R1-2 like blocklisted, not R1-3 like trimmed. Failing input: matchers:[{id:L1,kind:literal-line,value:"",stream:combined,polarity:present-in-red}] -> current output tags matcher-value-empty as R1-3; expected R1-2 per §1.3 rule 1. This choice is pinned into 3 committed regressions (red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs:219-221, red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts:298), so it is a systematic mistag, not a slip.

[codex host-B #2, orchestrator-verified] An empty literal value is tagged R1-3 but the spec assigns it R1-2. Section 1.6's R1-3 trigger enumeration covers a value LONGER than maxMatcherLen or carrying leading/trailing whitespace - it does not cover an empty value. Section 1.3 rule 1 explicitly requires value to be non-empty, and rule-1 failures are R1-2. red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs currently pins the wrong tag, which freezes the error. Fix the tag and the fixture.

[codex host-B #4, orchestrator-verified against spec text] greenExempt:false on a non-present-in-red matcher is accepted; it must reject. Section 1.1 states greenExempt is 'legal ONLY on polarity present-in-red matchers (any other polarity CARRYING IT is rejected)' - the test is whether the field is PRESENT, not whether it is true. The implementer's documented ambiguity resolution 5 reasoned that false cannot change assertion identity under section 0.4 and therefore accepted it; that reasoning is wrong on this clause. Reject on presence regardless of value, and add the fixture.

[codex host-B #5, orchestrator-verified] testCaseRef is never matched against the adapter's registered testCaseRefPattern. Section 1.2 (argv resolution) states: match testCaseRef against testCaseRefPattern; no match rejects R1-5. This is envelope-decidable - the pattern lives in the resolved policy registry and the testCaseRef is in the envelope - so it belongs in the same R1-5 check that already validates adapter registration. Failing input: adapterId npm-script@1 with testCaseRef 'free-form:not-derived' currently returns ok:true.
